events.title: SF × MIT Hack Day: Peptides
events.description:
Round two of the SF × MIT hack days, this time on peptides. Sundai Club builds at MIT, we build at AGI House SF.
Peptides are short chains of amino acids. GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide are peptides, and they've become some of the best-selling medicines in the world. A model can propose thousands of candidate sequences in an afternoon. The hard part is knowing which ones will bind their target, hold up in the body and stay safe, and that checking is the job we want agents doing: run the simulation, grade the result, get better each run.
Tracks:
Peptide design: agents that propose sequences against a target and score them with structure prediction and docking before anything gets synthesized.
Evidence engine: search and grade the published human data on peptides, from trials to adverse event

events.title: After Tokens
events.description:
After Tokens
The AI Economy Infrastructure Conference

What happens after the model call?
Tokens tell you what the model consumed. They don't tell you what a customer can use, when an agent should stop, or how a contract becomes a limit in your code.
After Tokens is about the infrastructure that answers those questions: metering, credits, entitlements, pricing, billing, and the systems that keep them in sync.
If you've had to meter an agent run, figure out what breaks when you move from tokens to credits, or check entitlements without slowing down the request, this day is for you.
One day, in person, in San Francisco: technical talks, architecture breakdowns, and lessons from systems running in production, aimed at the people who write the code.
